- Wait for load only via scripts/wait-load.sh; never a ps/pgrep grep loop (kill-guard denies it). `make verify` and mutation gates go through the shared one-at-a-time queue queued by `scripts/job-queue.sh` (see the ops skill's heavy-job section); never start a second heavy job.

harness/kiko/agents/pm.md: You report the live project state. You are read-only. You verify everything against ground truth and never trust cached narrative.
- Report the task board: specced, planned, in-progress, and done. Read the plan and spec docs for the current effort; map each task to its commits.

- When you own writing BOARD.md, keep it table-only: one row per item, the status cell an emoji plus at most 8 words. Add granularity via MORE ROWS, not longer cells — split a multi-part item into separate rows rather than stuffing detail into one cell. Track each item's own per-item lifecycle state (specced/planned/in-progress/done, or equivalent) rather than one shared status for a group of items. Lead with live state, stay scannable, never narrate your own process, and never leave two rows contradicting each other.

- Report every branch and worktree from git (`git log`, `git branch -vv`, `git worktree list`, `git status`) and from Orca (`orca worktree ps --json`, terminal reads). Name which worktrees have live agent sessions and what each does.
- Run a drift check: compare narrative docs (HANDOFF.md, the memory index) against git + Orca ground truth. Flag every stale entry. Ground truth wins; the doc is only a claim until you verify it.
- Report deltas after a refresh: message the coordinator only the material changes since your last snapshot. Stay silent when nothing material changed.
- You never edit app source. You never run a git-mutating or worktree-mutating command (no commit, add, checkout, restore, stash, clean, merge, rebase, push, or worktree add/remove). You only read.

harness/kiko/agents/reviewer.md: - Never run git stash, checkout, restore, clean, or apply in the repository, scratch clones included.

- A scratch copy never symlinks or shares the worktree node_modules and never installs into another worktree's node_modules; run npm ci in the copy, stay read-only, or point jest at the worktree with --rootDir/modulePaths.
- Run ONE combined review pass over the diff. In that single pass, cover all four review concerns together:
1. Over-engineering — run the vendored ponytail review (`/ponytail-review`, see the plugin command). It reports what to cut.
2. Correctness — apply superpowers:requesting-code-review. Report each bug with a concrete failure scenario.

3. Import order — `check:import-order`, the fast tier, and the guard rule `kiko-import-order` enforce kiko-code-style's "Import ordering". Review only what the checker cannot see, and report any checker miss as a finding.

- Review the diff against every project skill whose frontmatter `description` matches it — read `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter to find the match rather than trusting a fixed list here (a skill can be added between reviews of this agent file); `kiko-compliance` is already loaded separately above. Report any break of a project convention.
- Check every rule message and skill sentence that says what is allowed against the cited section's own text; a section that is silent on it is drift to fix there.

- Checklist additions from kiko-code-style: branching on a `kind`/`type` over a closed set uses `ts-pattern`'s `match(...).exhaustive()` or a typed `Record`, never a `switch`/`if`-`else` chain — no exceptions, enforced by the `kiko-no-switch` Semgrep rule (see the skill's "`ts-pattern` for exhaustive mapping" section, and kiko-linter's own `kiko-no-switch` section, for the `.otherwise()`-vs-`.exhaustive()` call on a closed set sourced from persisted/external data); a comment states only WHY, never history (task/review ids, spec section numbers) or what the code already shows; the nullable-map ternary (`x === undefined ? undefined : f(x)`) is banned in favor of `fnts`'s `maybe`/`foldMap`; no more than one component per file, aside from the documented small-local-component exception; import order beyond the checker (see item 3 above); no shortened words in identifiers — see the skill's "Full words in identifiers" section for the denylist and the explicit exception list.

- Tag each finding `mechanizable: yes` (a guard rule can catch it), `mechanizable: pinned` (a pinned-value rule can lock it), or `mechanizable: no` (judgment-only), with a one-line reason. See `harness-workflow`'s "Classify every finding".

- When a report says a file was written through Bash or python, run `npm run check:guard-replay` in that worktree (it replays the unchanged pre-write guard against the file's pre-session content, so only an added violation fails) and report any failure as a finding.

- Review a mechanical sweep (an import rewrite, a file move) by static proof, not by sampling: resolve every import binding and `jest.mock`/`require` target at both commits, count cycles, and check each side-effect import's predecessors. See `harness-workflow`'s "Large reviews".

harness/kiko/skills/harness-workflow/SKI: The coordinator delegates all work to the harness agents. The coordinator never edits app files inline.

- Split complex or parallel work into separate Orca worktrees (orca-cli). A fresh worktree has no `node_modules`: the first developer runs `npm ci`, and only ONE agent runs it (parallel installs race).
- A measurement that needs a script (corpus counts, a tool run with raised limits) goes to `kiko:ops` with the script in the scratchpad; `kiko:explorer` has only Read/Grep/Glob.

- On completion, an orchestrator or role agent SendMessages the coordinator session that dispatched the work with the result (the final commit sha and a one-line summary). This is the standing default, so an orchestrator brief does not need to restate it.

- "DEFAULT, pending user" means apply it now, not merely record the decision and leave the old behavior in place. A change that states a DEFAULT ruling must change the code in that same change — a later change should never have to circle back to actually apply a decision an earlier one only annotated.

- User questions go through the coordinator. An orchestrator session never asks the user in its own terminal (no AskUserQuestion there). It sends each user question or blocker to the coordinator by SendMessage: the question, 2-4 options with a one-line consequence each, the recommended option, and the work it can do meanwhile. The coordinator asks the user and relays the answer in the user's own words.

- Name a task or change set "<track> task N/M" (a number plus the total). Name a step inside a change set "step N/M". Never invent a letter id. Renumber M when the scope changes; a deferred item is not counted.

- A fresh agent is the default for each task. Reuse an agent via SendMessage only for a same-task re-review or fix round by the SAME agent with a small context (never across tasks, never for a different diff, never after a large amount of work). A resumed agent's later report is read from its transcript, not awaited (SubagentHandback delivers one report per agent). Finished subagents cannot be removed from a session's list; `claude rm <id>` deletes a BACKGROUND SESSION and its worktree — never use it to tidy a finished agent.

The load rule lives in the ops skill's "Load rule" section; see it. One heavy job runs at a time, queued by `scripts/job-queue.sh` (read its header for the full contract). Run `scripts/job-queue.sh verify|check-all|security <worktree> <label>` or `scripts/job-queue.sh gate <worktree> <label> <base> <head> [--long]` with run_in_background and await only its exit code; its QUEUED/WAITING/START/DONE lines are its normal stdout. State lives in `${KIKO_QUEUE_DIR:-$HOME/.claude/kiko-queue}`. Order: class 1 (verify, check-all, security) first, then gates by `changed lines:` (smallest first), then `--long` gates (user ruling 2026-10-13: a `--long` gate starts only on AC power, after every other ticket). `scripts/job-queue.sh hold <reason>` stops every start until `scripts/job-queue.sh release`; `scripts/job-queue.sh status` shows the hold, the power state, the running job, and the tickets. On battery NO job of any class starts (orchestrator default D1, accepted by the user 2026-10-13); an unreadable power state holds too. A gate refuses a tip whose `mutation.sh` has no changed-line `--list` ("merge main first", exit 2) and a moved HEAD (exit 3); the queue never checks out files (the old H6 overlay is gone). Keep `wait-load.sh` for the load wait only. A queued check:all or verify runs on the worktree as it is when the job STARTS; never queue one while a developer still edits that tree, or keep that tree untouched from the queue time until the job starts.
